en: To blink with only one eye as a message, signal, or suggestion, usually with an implication of conspiracy. (When transitive, the object m…
To gleam fitfully or intermittently; to twinkle; to flicker.
An act of winking (a blinking of only one eye), or a message sent by winking.
A brief period of sleep; especially forty winks.

Cognate with Middle Low German winken (“to blink, wink”), German winken (“to nod, beckon, make a sign”). ex.en: With this noise, I couldn't sleep a wink.
ex.ja: この騒音で一睡も出来なかった。

ex.en: I didn't sleep a wink last night.
ex.ja: 私は昨晩一睡もしなかった。

ex.en: Last night I did not get a wink of sleep.
ex.ja: ゆうべは一睡もしなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 wincian（目を閉じる）から。「ウインク」。forty winks（うたた寝）。

en: Of or relating to astronomy.
Very large; of vast measure.

astronomical.ety: Attested since at least 1550, from Middle French astronomique or directly from Latin astronomicus, from Ancient Greek ἀστρονομικός (astronomikós).

ex.en: The figure will be astronomical.
ex.ja: 数字は天文学的なものだろう。

en: One's dress; what one wears; one's clothes.
The single horn of a goat, deer or stag.
To clothe or adorn.

attire.ety:
The verb is from Middle English atyren, atiren, from Old French atirier (“to equip”), from a- + tire (“rank”), akin to German Zier (“ornament”) and Old Norse tírr (“glory, renown”).
The noun is from Middle English atir, from the verb.

ex.en: What kind of women's attire does Tom like?
ex.ja: トムは女性のどんなファッションが好き？

note.ja: 古フランス語 atirier（整える）から。「服装」。

en: A person’s own handwriting, especially the signature of a famous or admired person.
A person's signature used as a mark of formal approval.
Written in the author’s own handwriting.
Made by the artist himself or herself; authentic.
To sign, or write one’s name or signature on a book, etc.
To write something in one's own handwriting.

autograph.ety: From Latin autographum, in turn from Ancient Greek αὐτόγραφον (autógraphon, “a writing in one’s own hand”). Equivalent to auto- + -graph.

ex.en: Star baseball players are often asked for autographs.
ex.ja: スターの野球選手はよくサインを求められる。

ex.en: Could I have your autograph on this book?
ex.ja: この本にサインしてもらえませんか。

ex.en: I can give you an autograph if you want.
ex.ja: サイン書いてやってもいいぞ。

note.ja: auto（自分）+ graph（書く）。自分で書いたもの →「サイン・自筆」。

en: The pin or spindle on which a wheel revolves, or which revolves with a wheel.
A transverse bar or shaft connecting the opposite wheels of a car or carriage; an axletree.

axle.ety:
From Middle English axel, axle, eaxle, from Old English eaxl (“shoulder, armpit”), from Proto-West Germanic *ahslu (“shoulder”), from Proto-Germanic *ahslō (“shoulder”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs-l-eh₂, from *h₂eḱs- (“axis, axle”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian acsle (“shoulder”), Dutch oksel (“armpit”), German Achsel (“armpit”), Swedish axel (“shoulder”), Latin axilla (“armpit”), Latin axis (“axle”) (whence English axis, atelier, and via Latin āla English ala, aisle), Ancient Greek ἄξων (áxōn) (whence English axo-, axon),
Greek άξονας (áxonas, “axle”), Sanskrit अक्ष (ákṣa, “axle”), San

ex.en: Wheels turn on axles.
ex.ja: 車輪は車軸で回転する。

note.ja: 北欧語 öxull（車軸）から。axis と同じ祖先。

en: A cereal of the species Hordeum vulgare or its grains, often used as food or to make beer and other malted drinks.
The seed of Job's tears (Coix lacryma-jobi).

barley.ety: From Middle English barly, barli, from Old English bærlīċ (“barley-like”, adjective) (later referring to barley itself and grain crops of similar appearance), from bere (“barley”) (compare Scots bere (“six-rowed barley”)), from Proto-Germanic *baraz (compare Old Norse barr), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰers- (“spike, prickle”). Equivalent to bere + -ly. See English brew.

ex.en: Barley is our main product.
ex.ja: 大麦は我国の主産物である。

ex.en: Will you drink barley tea?
ex.ja: 麦茶のむ？

ex.en: Do you drink barley tea?
ex.ja: 麦茶のむ？

note.ja: 古英語 bærlic（大麦の）から。barn（大麦の家 → 納屋）と同じ bere。

Something derived from a botanical, especially herbal, source.

ex.ja: 私たちは植物園で多くの珍しい植物を見ました。

ex.en: We saw many unusual plants in the botanical garden.
ex.ja: 私たちは植物園で多くの珍しい植物を見ました。

en: A boast or boasting; bragging; ostentatious pretence or self-glorification.
The thing which is boasted of.
To boast; to talk with excessive pride about what one has, is able to do, or has done; often as an attempt to popularize oneself.
Excellent; first-rate.

brag.ety: From Middle English braggen (“to make a loud noise; to speak boastfully”) of uncertain origin. Possibly related to the Middle English adjective brag (“prideful; spirited”), which is probably of Celtic origin; or from Old Norse bragr (“best; foremost; poetry”); or through Old English from Old Norse braka (“to creak”).

ex.en: He'll be bragging about it soon enough.
ex.ja: すぐ、自慢するんだから。

ex.en: He bragged of having won the victory.
ex.ja: 彼は勝利を得たことを自慢した。

ex.en: I'm tired of listening to your bragging.
ex.ja: 君の自慢話はもう聞き飽きた。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「自慢する」。

en: An escape from prison.
An escape from any restrictive or confining situation.
Of a book, film, or other work: leading its author to sudden mainstream success.
Splitting a signal into several signals.

breakout.ety: Deverbal from break out. The video game genre is named after Breakout, the first game of this kind, released in 1976 by Atari.

ex.en: It became his breakout work.
ex.ja: それは彼の出世作となった。

note.ja: break out（脱出する・勃発する）の名詞化。「脱走・ブレイク」。

en: Instantly appealing and memorable.
Contagious; catching.

ex.ja: この歌、覚えやすいね。

en: Of, relating to, consisting of, or used in a ceremony.
Used only for the purpose of ceremony; symbolic.
A ceremony, or series of ceremonies, prescribed by ritual.

ceremonial.ety: From Middle English cerymonial, from Latin caerimōniālis. Morphologically ceremony + -al or -ial.

ex.en: I drank ceremonial sake with gold leaf in it at the new year.
ex.ja: お正月には金箔入りのお神酒を頂きました。

note.ja: ceremony（儀式）+ -al。ラテン語 caerimonia（神聖な儀式）。「儀式の」。

A bill to be paid, particularly in a restaurant.

ex.ja: 旅行代理店の人は、旅行者用小切手を持っていってはどうかと提案した。

note.ja: check のイギリスのつづり。「小切手」。

en: The art of creating, arranging and recording the dance movements of a work, such as a ballet.
The art of creating and arranging sequences of movement for performances of any kind, such as in fight choreography.

choreography.ety:
Reshaping of earlier choregraphy, a borrowing from French chorégraphie, from Ancient Greek χορεία (khoreía, “dance”) + -γραφίᾱ (-graphíā, “written form (of a word, etc.), spelling”). By surface analysis, choreo- + -graphy.
Both choregraphy and choreography replaced earlier chorography in the dance sense (from χορός (khorós, “dance ring, round dance”) + -γραφία (-graphía); compare Greek χορογραφία (chorografía)), which had been used in 1710 as a translation of the same French term.

ex.en: The choreography is quite simple.
ex.ja: 振り付けはとてもシンプルだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khoreia（合唱舞踊）+ graphia（書くこと）。「踊りを書き記すこと」→「振り付け」。chorus と同じ。

en: Fruit (especially peach) whose flesh adheres strongly to the pit.
Adherence; attachment; devotion.
To hold very tightly, as to not fall off.
To adhere to an object, without being affixed, in such a way as to follow its contours. Used especially of fabrics and films.
Imitative of a high-pitched ringing sound.

cling.ety: From Middle English clingen, from Old English clingan (“to adhere”), from Proto-West Germanic *klingan, from Proto-Germanic *klinganą. Cognate with Danish klynge (“to cluster, to crowd”). Compare clump.

ex.en: The boy is clinging to his mother.
ex.ja: その男の子は母親にしがみついている。

ex.en: That child was clinging to his mother.
ex.ja: その子供は母親にぴったりとくっついていた。

ex.en: My wet clothes clung to my body.
ex.ja: ぬれた服が体にくっついた。

note.ja: 古英語 clingan（くっつく）から。「しがみつく」。clench、clinch と同系。

en: To occupy exactly the same space.
To occur at the same time.

coincide.ety: From French coïncider, from Medieval Latin coincidere, from con- + incidere, from in- (“into, to”) + cadere (“to fall, fall down, drop”).

ex.en: Lunch is at 12:00 to coincide with the Technical Group.
ex.ja: 昼食は、テクニカルグループも交えて、十二時からです。

ex.en: My birthday coincides with yours.
ex.ja: 私の誕生日とあなたの誕生日が、偶然重なる。

ex.en: It's clear that our arguments don't coincide at all.
ex.ja: 我々の議論が噛み合わないのは明らかだ。

note.ja: co（共に）+ incidere（落ちる）。「同じ所に落ちる」→「同時に起こる・一致する」。coincidence と同じ。

en: To honour the memory of someone or something with a ceremony or object.
To serve as a memorial to someone or something.

commemorate.ety: First attested in 1599; borrowed from Latin commemorātus, perfect passive participle of commemorō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Sporadic usage of the adjective up until Early Modern English.

ex.en: They were erected to commemorate a certain event or to tell an ancestral legend.
ex.ja: ある出来事を記念したり先祖の伝説を伝えるために建てられたものであった。

en: Happening at the same time; simultaneous.
Belonging to the same period; contemporary.
One who, or that which, concurs; a joint or contributory cause.
One pursuing the same course, or seeking the same objects; hence, a rival; an opponent.

concurrent.ety: From Middle English concurrent, from Old French concurrent, from Latin concurrēns, present active participle of concurrō (“happen at the same time”), from con- (“with”) + currō (“run”).

note.ja: con（共に）+ cur（走る）+ rent。一緒に走る →「同時に起こる・並行の」。

en: Any of the predatory amphibious reptiles of the family Crocodylidae; (loosely) a crocodilian, any species of the order Crocodilia, which …
A long line or procession of people (especially children) walking together.

crocodile.ety: Inherited from Middle English cocodrill, cokadrill, cokedril, from Old French cocodril (modern French crocodile), from Medieval Latin cocodrillus, from Latin crocodilus, from Ancient Greek κροκόδειλος (krokódeilos). The word was later refashioned after the Latin and Greek forms. Doublet of krokodil.

ex.en: Don't be taken in by her crocodile tears.
ex.ja: 彼女の空涙にだまされるな。

ex.en: A crocodile ate a dog.
ex.ja: ワニが犬を食べた。

ex.en: She shed crocodile tears over his death.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼の死にそら涙を流した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 krokodeilos（小石のミミズ）から。ナイル川のワニが石の上で日光浴したことから。

A container that absorbs and collects (retains) liquid or waste material, similar to a diaper (noun sense 1).
To put diapers on someone.
To draw geometrical or floral patterns, as upon cloth.

en: To eat; to eat dinner or supper.
To give a dinner to; to furnish with the chief meal; to feed.

dine.ety: From Middle English dynen, from Old French disner (“to dine, eat the main meal of the day”), from Vulgar Latin *disiūnāre (“to eat breakfast”), from *disieiūnāre (“to break the fast”), from Late Latin, from dis- + iēiūnō (“to fast”), from Latin ieiūnus.

To destroy, make disappear.
a form of film punctuation in which there is a gradual transition from one scene to the next

dissolve.ety: Recorded since c. 1374 (displacing Old English toliesan) as Middle English dissolven, from Latin dissolvere (“to loosen up, break apart”) but with the sense from Anglo-Norman dissoldre (variant of Old French dissoudre), itself from dis- (“apart”) + solvere (“to loose, loosen”). ex.en: Sugar will dissolve quickly in a glass of water.
ex.ja: 砂糖は、すぐにグラスの水の中で溶けるだろう。

ex.ja: 砂糖は熱いコーヒーに入れると溶ける。

ex.en: Dissolve sugar in hot water.
ex.ja: 砂糖をお湯で溶かしなさい。

ex.ja: 彼は音楽を聴いて気を紛らした。

ex.en: They diverted the river to supply water somewhere else.
ex.ja: 彼らは他のところへ水を供給するために川の流れの向きを変えた。

en: Arousing doubt; questionable; open to suspicion.
In disbelief; wavering, uncertain, or hesitating in opinion; inclined to doubt; undecided.

dubious.ety: From Latin dubius; like doubt, from Latin duo (cognate to English two), implying “two alternatives” (yes or no, true or false, etc.).

ex.en: He also brought out one more dubious conclusion.
ex.ja: そしてもう一つは疑わしい結論を出した。

ex.en: Students are expected to stay away from dubious places.
ex.ja: 学生たるものはいかがわしい場所にちかづかない方がよい。

ex.en: Tom was still dubious.
ex.ja: トムはまだ怪訝そうだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 dubius（ふたつに迷う）から。duo（2）。「疑わしい」。doubt と同じ。

en: In an eager manner.

eagerly.ety: From Middle English egrely, egerly; equivalent to eager + -ly.

ex.en: I've been waiting eagerly for this moment.
ex.ja: この瞬間を待ち望んでいました。

ex.en: It would be good for you to study eagerly.
ex.ja: あなたは懸命に勉強をすればよい。

ex.en: They eagerly supported his new policy.
ex.ja: 彼等は熱心に新政策を支持した。

note.ja: eager（熱心な）+ -ly。eager はラテン語 acer（鋭い）から。「熱心に」。

en: Of or pertaining to the church.

ecclesiastical.ety: From Middle English ecclesiasticall, ecclesiasticalle, from Latin ecclēsiasticus + -al. By surface analysis, ecclesiastic + -al or ecclesiast + -ical.

en: Educated or informed.
Made aware of something.
Someone who has been introduced to the mysteries of some activity, religion especially Buddhism

ex.en: He holds a very enlightened attitude toward working women.
ex.ja: 彼は働く婦人たちに対してとても理解のある態度をとっている。

ex.en: He enlightened me on how I should attack the subject.

ex.en: The Buddha became enlightened under a Bo tree in Bodh Gaya.
ex.ja: 釈迦はブッダガヤの菩提樹の下で悟りを開いた。

ex.ja: 佐藤さんは疲れ切って倒れた。

ex.ja: 水夫は仲間の水夫が力尽きて沈むのを目撃した。

The state of being expected.

en: The natural pattern of ridges on the tips of human fingers, unique to each individual.
The pattern left on a surface where an uncovered fingertip has touched, especially as used to identify the person who touched the surface.
To take somebody's fingerprints.
To identify something uniquely by a combination of measurements.

ex.en: Tom carefully wiped his fingerprints off the knife.
ex.ja: トムは念入りにナイフから指紋を拭き取った。

ex.en: The police said they found Tom's fingerprints there.
ex.ja: 警察が言うには、トムの指紋をそこで見つけたんだって。

ex.en: The police dusted the van for fingerprints.
ex.ja: 警察はバンの指紋を採取した。

note.ja: finger（指）+ print（跡）。「指紋」。

en: Anything broad and flexible that hangs loose, or that is attached by one side or end and is easily moved.
A hinged leaf.
To move (something broad and loose) up and down.
To move loosely back and forth.

flap.ety: From Middle English flap, flappe (“a slap; blow; buffet; fly-flap; something flexible or loose; flap”), related to Saterland Frisian Flappert (“wing, flipper”), Middle Dutch flabbe (“a blow; slap on the face; fly-flap; flap”) (modern Dutch flap (“flap”)), Middle Low German flabbe, vlabbe, flebbe, from the verb (see below). Related also to English flab and flabby.

ex.en: She flapped at the fly with a newspaper.
ex.ja: 彼女は新聞でハエをピシャっとたたいた。

ex.en: The bird flapped its wings.
ex.ja: 鳥が翼をはばたかせた。

ex.en: He flapped the flies away.
ex.ja: 彼はハエをたたいて追い払った。

note.ja: 擬音的な語。「パタパタ」→「はためく・羽ばたく」。

The tales, superstitions etc. of any particular group or community.

ex.en: Hanako's favorite anime is "Night on the Galactic Railroad".
ex.ja: 花子ちゃんの好きなアニメは「銀河鉄道の夜」です。

en: One who gardens; one who grows plants or cultivates a garden.

gardener.ety:
From Middle English gardener, either calqued or loaned from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French gardinier.
See garden, and compare German Gärtner (“gardener”), which is equivalent to a derivative of the German cognate to English garden, Garten (“garden”), + -er.
Displaced native Old English wyrtweard (effectively "wortward").

ex.en: I had the gardener plant some trees.
ex.ja: 植木屋さんに木を何本か植えてもらった。

ex.en: A gardener was called in to design the garden.
ex.ja: 造園のために庭師が呼ばれた。

ex.en: A garden is the reflection of the gardener.
ex.ja: 庭は庭師を映す鏡だ。

note.ja: garden（庭）+ -er。「庭師」。

en: Joy; happiness; great delight, especially from one's own good fortune or from another's misfortune.
Music; minstrelsy; entertainment.
To sing a glee (unaccompanied part song).

glee.ety:

Cognate with Scots gle, glie, glew (“game, play, sport, mirth, joy, rejoicing, entertainment, melody, music”), Icelandic glý (“joy, glee, gladness”), Ancient Greek χλεύη (khleúē, “joke, jest, scorn”). A poetic word in Middle English, the word was obsolete by 1500, but revived late 18c.

ex.en: Are you going to join the glee club?
ex.ja: グリークラブに入るつもりなの？

ex.en: I'm a member of the glee club.
ex.ja: 私はグリークラブのメンバーです。

en: Grazeland.
The action of animals eating, mainly of grass in a field or on other grassland.

ex.en: Cattle were grazing in the field.
ex.ja: 牛が野原で草をはんでいた。

ex.ja: 羊が牧草地で草をはんでいた。

en: The discharging a firearm.
The firing of guns; gunfire.

ex.en: I'm surprised no one else heard the gunshots.
ex.ja: 私以外の誰も銃声を聞いていないことに驚いた。

ex.en: While he was giving the speech, the sound of a gunshot could be heard.
ex.ja: ちょうど彼が演説していた時に、銃声がひびき渡った。

ex.en: My eardrums burst because of the gunshot.
ex.ja: 銃声のせいで鼓膜が破れた。

note.ja: gun（銃）+ shot（発射）。「銃声」。

en: Passed on as an inheritance, by last will or intestate.
Of a title, honor or right: legally granted to somebody's descendant after that person's death.
A hereditary ruler; a hereditary peer in the House of Lords.

hereditary.ety: Inherited from Middle English hereditarie, from Latin hērēditārius, from hērēditās (“inheritance”), from hērēs (“heir”).

ex.en: My baby has a hereditary disease.
ex.ja: 子供は遺伝病を持っています。

note.ja: ラテン語 hereditas（相続）から。heres（相続人）。「遺伝性の・世襲の」。heir、heritage と同じ。

en: A gap in a series, making it incomplete.
An interruption, break, pause or absence.

hiatus.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin hiātus (“opening”) (mid-16th century), from hiō (“stand open, yawn”).

ex.en: The band is on hiatus.
ex.ja: そのバンドはただいまお休みです。

note.ja: ラテン語 hiatus（裂け目・すき間）から。hiare（口を開ける）。「中断」。

en: A house together with surrounding land and buildings, especially on a farm; the property comprising these.
A parcel of land in the interior of North America, usually 160 acres, that was distributed to settlers from Europe or eastern North Ameri…
To acquire or settle on land as a homestead.
To appropriate an unowned, scarce means, and thereby gain ownership of it.

homestead.ety: From Middle English hamstede, hemstede (attested in placenames), from Old English hāmstede (“homestead”), from Proto-West Germanic *haimastadi (“homestead”). By surface analysis, home + stead. Cognate with Old Frisian hāmstede, hēmstede (“homestead”), Dutch heemstede (“homestead”), German Heimstatt, Heimstätte (“homestead”), Swedish hemstad (“homestead”), Old Icelandic heimstǫð (“homestead”). Doublet of Hampstead and Hempstead.

en: In a horrible way; very badly.
To an extreme degree or extent.

horribly.ety: From Middle English horribly, horribely, horribliche, horriblelyche, equivalent to horrible + -ly.

ex.en: During his illness, he fell away horribly.
ex.ja: 病気の間に彼はひどくやせた。

ex.en: My father is horribly choosy about food.
ex.ja: 父は食べ物にすごくうるさいんです。

ex.en: "It's raining horribly hard. You didn't get wet?" "No, I'm okay."
ex.ja: 「ひどい雨だね。濡れなかった？」「うん、大丈夫」

en: Power derived from the motion of a horse.
A nonmetric unit of power with various definitions, commonly the mechanical horsepower, approximately equal to 745.7 watts.

horsepower.ety:
From horse + power: the unit was originally defined as the amount of power that a horse could provide.
Both non-metric and metric units of power were derived from effectively identical measurements of the power a draught horse could sustain over several hours, with the difference in watts solely due to different rounding errors to express that power in round numbers in the original non-SI units (ft·lbf/min and kgf⋅m/s respectively).

ex.en: My car is deficient in horsepower.
ex.ja: 私の車は馬力が足らない。

note.ja: horse（馬）+ power（力）。ジェームズ・ワットが蒸気機関の性能を馬の力と比べたことから。

en: A color, or shade of color; tint; dye.
The characteristic related to the light frequency that appears in the color, for instance red, yellow, green, cyan, blue or magenta.

hue.ety: From Middle English hewe, from Old English hīew (“appearance, form, species, kind; apparition; hue, color; beauty; figure of speech”), from Proto-West Germanic *hiwi, from Proto-Germanic *hiwją (“hue, form, shape, appearance; mildew”), from Proto-Indo-European *kew-, *ḱew- (“skin, colour of the skin”) or *ḱey- (“grey, dark shade”). Cognate with Swedish hy (“complexion, skin”), Norwegian hy (“fluff, mold, skin”), Icelandic hégómi (“vanity”), Gothic 𐌷𐌹𐍅𐌹 (hiwi, “form, show, appearance”). Compare also Sanskrit छवि (chavi, “cuticle, skin, hide; beauty, splendour”); Irish ceo (“fog”), Tocharian B k

ex.en: Her dresses show most of the hues of the rainbow.
ex.ja: 彼女のドレスはにじの色のほとんどがそろっている。

note.ja: 古英語 hīw（形・色）から。「色合い」。

en: The faculty of thinking, judging, abstract reasoning, and conceptual understanding; the cognitive faculty.
The capacity of that faculty (in a particular person).

intellect.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin intellēctus (“understanding, intellect”), from Latin intellegō (“understand; reason”), from inter (“between, among”) + legō (“read”), with connotation of bind.

ex.en: He is a man of intellect.
ex.ja: 彼は知的な人です。

ex.en: It is beyond the boundaries of human intellect.
ex.ja: それは人知の限界を越えている。

ex.en: Opinion is ultimately determined by feelings, and not by the intellect.
ex.ja: 意見は究極的には感情によって決定されるのであって、理知によってではない。

note.ja: intel（間で）+ lect（選ぶ）。物事の間から選び分ける力 →「知性・知力」。

en: to switch (each of two things)
to mutually give and receive (something); to exchange
An act of interchanging.
A highway junction in which traffic may change from one road to another without crossing a stream of traffic.

interchange.ety: From Old French entrechange, by surface analysis, inter- + change.

note.ja: inter（互いに）+ change（交換する）。「交換・インターチェンジ」。

en: A holy war undertaken by Muslims.
A personal spiritual struggle for self-improvement or against evil.
To participate in a jihad.

note.ja: アラビア語 jihād（努力・奮闘）から。「聖戦」。

en: A rounded protuberance, especially one arising from a flat surface; a fleshy lump or caruncle.
A rounded control switch that can be turned on its axis, designed to be operated by the fingers.
protrude
furnish or produce with a knob, knobble

knob.ety:
From Middle English knobbe, from Middle Low German knobbe (“knob, knot in wood, bud”), probably ultimately from a variant of Proto-Germanic *knappô (“knob, lump”), one of several kn- words related to *knudaną (“to knead”).
Compare Middle Dutch knobbe, cnoppe, Middle Low German knobbe (“knob, knot in wood”), knubbe, Dutch knop (“knob, button, bud”), Old Frisian knopp, knapp, Old High German knopf (“bud, pommel of a sword, knot, loop”), Middle High German knospe, German Knopf (“button, knob”), Knospe (“bud”), Danish knap (“button”), knop (“knob, button, bud”), Faroese knappur (“button”), Iceland

ex.en: Turn the knob and open the door.
ex.ja: ノブを回して、ドアをあけなさい。

ex.en: I tried the knob.
ex.ja: 私はドアの取っ手を回した。

ex.en: Twist that knob to the right and the box will open.
ex.ja: その取っ手を右にねじると箱は開きます。

note.ja: 中世低地ドイツ語 knobbe（こぶ）から。「取っ手・つまみ」。

en: A temporary failure; a slip.
A decline or fall in standards.
To fall away gradually; to subside.
To fall into error or heresy.

lapse.ety: From Middle French laps, from Latin lāpsus, from lābī (“to slip”). Doublet of lapsus.

ex.en: He lapsed into despair after that accident.
ex.ja: 彼はその事故のあと自暴自棄に陥った。

ex.en: I am a lapsed vegetarian.
ex.ja: 私は菜食主義者をやめたの。

note.ja: ラテン語 lapsus（滑ること）から。labi（滑る）。「うっかりした失敗」→「（時の）経過・失効」。collapse（共に滑り落ちる）と同じ。

en: The act, or occupation, of one who launders; washing and ironing.
A book for keeping notes; a record book, a register.
A book or other scheme for keeping accounting records.
To record (something) in, or as if in, a ledger.
To use (a certain type of bait) in bottom fishing.

The word is cognate with Saterland Frisian Lägger (“floor board, joist, plank”), West Frisian lêger (“beam, plank”), Dutch legger (“daybook; layer”) (from leggen (“to lay”), liggen (“to lie down”)), and is related to English ledge, lie (“to be

ex.ja: 事務員は原簿に記入した。

ex.en: There are many questionable points in this ledger.
ex.ja: この帳簿には不明朗な点がたくさんある。

note.ja: 中英語 legger（置かれた本）から。lay、lie と同系。「台帳」。

en: A block of bread after baking.
Any solid block of food, such as meat or sugar.
To do nothing, to be idle.

ex.ja: 今朝、彼女はパンを１個買った。

ex.ja: 私は朝食に食パンを１つかいました。

ex.en: My mother bought a loaf of bread.
ex.ja: 母はパンを一個買った。

note.ja: 古英語 hlāf（パン）から。lord（パンの番人）、lady（パンをこねる人）にも含まれる。

en: Credentials: the combination of a user's identification and password used to enter a computer, program, network, etc.
The process or an instance of logging in.

ex.en: Your login attempt was not successful. Please try again.
ex.ja: ログインできませんでした。再度ログインしてください。

note.ja: log in（記録に入る）の名詞化。log はもと船の速度を測る丸太 →「航海日誌」→「記録」。

Synonym of sack, the plundering of a city, particularly during war.
Synonym of plunder, to seize by violence, particularly during the capture of a city during war or (video games) after successful combat.
To rifle through a dead body and the deceased's belongings, taking anything worth stealing.

loot.ety: Borrowed from Hindi लूट (lūṭ, “booty”), either from Sanskrit लोप्त्र (loptra, “booty, stolen property”) or लुण्ट् (luṇṭ, “to rob, plunder”). The figurative meaning developed in American English in the 1920s, resulting in a generalized meaning by the 1950s.

ex.en: Tom is playing the lute.
ex.ja: トムはリュートを弾いています。

ex.en: The thief outwitted the police and got away with his loot.
ex.ja: 泥棒は警官の裏をかいて盗品を持って逃げた。

ex.en: A government official's stately mansion was looted.
ex.ja: 政府役人の豪邸が略奪された。

en: To imitate, especially in order to ridicule.
To take on the appearance of another, for protection or camouflage.
A mime.
A comic who does impressions.
Pertaining to mimicry; imitative.
Mock, pretended.

From Latin mīmicus, from Ancient Greek μῑμικός (mīmikós, “belonging to mimes”), from μῖμος (mîmos, “imitator, actor”); see mime.

ex.en: Tests showed that Alex wasn't just mimicking.
ex.ja: 試してみると、アレックスは単に物まねをしているのではないことがわかった。

ex.en: A parrot can mimic a person's voice.
ex.ja: オウムは人の声を真似ることができる。

ex.en: Sport is frankly mimic warfare.
ex.ja: スポーツは率直に言って模擬的な戦闘である。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mimikos（まねの）から。mimos（物まね役者）。「まねる」。mime、meme と同じ。

en: aware (of something); attentive, heedful.
Of or pertaining to mindfulness; sustaining meta-attention of the contents of one's own mind in the present moment.
As much as can be held in one's mind at a time.

mindful.ety: From Middle English myndeful, myndefull, from Old English ġemyndful (“of good memory”), equivalent to mind + -ful.

ex.en: Tom was mindful of my warning.
ex.ja: トムは私の警告を忘れなかった。

ex.en: Be mindful of the differences between written and spoken language.
ex.ja: 書き言葉と話し言葉の違いを意識する。

ex.en: You must be mindful of your family responsibilities.
ex.ja: 君は家族扶養の責任を忘れてはならない。

en: A large painting, usually drawn on a wall.
Of or relating to a wall; on, or in, or against a wall.
Resembling a wall; perpendicular or steep.
To create a mural.

mural.ety: Borrowed from French mural, from Latin muralis, from murus (“wall”).

note.ja: ラテン語 murus（壁）から。「壁画」。

en: A greasy secretion with a powerful odour, produced in a glandular sac of the male musk deer and used in the manufacture of perfumes.
A similar secretion produced by the otter and the civet.
To perfume with musk.

musk.ety: From Middle English muske, borrowed from Old French musc, from Late Latin muscus, from Ancient Greek μόσχος (móskhos), from Middle Persian [script needed] (mwšk' /⁠muʃk⁠/) whence Persian مشک (mošk). Ultimately from Sanskrit मुष्क (muṣka, “testicle”), the shape of the gland of animals secreting the substance being compared to human testicles, a diminutive of मूष् (mūṣ, “mouse”), the shape of human testicles being compared to mice, from Proto-Indo-European *múHs (“mouse”). Cognate with mouse.

ex.en: Musk is one of the best scents.
ex.ja: 麝香の香りは最も良い香りの一つである。

ex.en: Elon Musk is a Nazi.
ex.ja: イーロン・マスクはナチスだ。

ex.en: The scent of musk is one of the best smells there is.
ex.ja: ムスクの香りは最も良い香りの一つです。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 mushk から。サンスクリット語で「陰嚢」の意とされ、ジャコウジカの香嚢の形から。

Synonym of decamillennium: a period of 10000 years.
Multifaceted, having innumerable elements.
Great in number; innumerable, multitudinous.

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ vent（来る）+ ur + ous。これから来ることに向かっていく →「冒険好きな・大胆な」。

en: Ammunition.
To load up on ammunition.

ammo.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *móyni
Proto-Italic *moini
Latin moene
Proto-Indo-European *-yétider.

Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin mūnitiōnemlbor.
Middle French munition
Middle French amunitionbor.
English ammunitionclip.
English ammo
Clipping of ammunition.

note.ja: ammunition の短縮。「弾薬」。

en: A collection of literary works, such as poems or short stories, especially a collection from various authors.
A work or series containing various stories with no direct relation to one another.

anthology.ety: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀνθολογία (anthología, “flower-gathering”), from ἀνθολογέω (anthologéō, “I gather flowers”), from ἄνθος (ánthos, “flower”) + λέγω (légō, “I gather, pick up, collect”), coined by Meleager of Gadara circa 60 BCE, originally as Στέφανος (στέφανος (stéphanos, “garland”)) to describe a collection of poetry, later retitled anthology – see Greek Anthology. Anthologiai were collections of small Greek poems and epigrams, because in Greek culture the flower symbolized the finer sentiments that only poetry can express. By surface analysis, antho- + -logy.

ex.en: I like both plays in our anthology very much.
ex.ja: 私たちの選集にある劇は２つともとても好きだ。

ex.en: He compiled a Japanese folklore anthology for use in schools.
ex.ja: 彼は日本の民話を教科書用に纏めた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 anthos（花）+ logia（集めること）。「花を摘み集めたもの」→「選集」。chrysanthemum（金の花 → 菊）と同じ anth。

en: In any way or manner whatever.
In any case. Used to indicate that a statement explains or supports a previous statement.
Random, careless, offhand, disorderly; done without thought or consideration.

anyhow.ety:

ex.en: We could not open the box anyhow.
ex.ja: どうしても箱が開かなかった。

ex.en: It might rain, but I'm going anyhow.
ex.ja: 雨は降るかもしれませんが、どうにかして行きます。

ex.en: It may rain, but I will go today anyhow.
ex.ja: 雨が降るかもしれないが、とにかく私は今日行きます。

note.ja: any（どんな）+ how（方法で）。「どんな方法でも」→「とにかく」。

en: An anthropoid of the superfamily Hominoidea, generally larger than monkeys and distinguished from them by having no tail.
A Hominoidea primate other than a human.
To behave like an ape.
To imitate or mimic, particularly to imitate poorly.

ape.ety:
From Middle English ape, from Old English apa (“ape, monkey”), from Proto-West Germanic *apō, from Proto-Germanic *apô (“monkey, ape”), possibly derived from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ep- (“water”), compare Proto-Celtic *abū (“river”) (hence English place name Avon, Irish abha, Welsh afon), if the word originally referred to a "water sprite".
Traditionally assumed to be an ancient loanword instead, ultimately probably from an unidentified non-Indo-European language of regions in Africa or Asia where monkeys are native.
Cognate with Scots aip (“ape”), West Frisian aap (“ape”), Dutch aap (“monkey,

ex.en: Apes rank above dogs in intelligence.
ex.ja: 類人猿は知的には犬より上位である。

ex.en: Why have the apes evolved more than other animals?
ex.ja: なぜ類人猿は他の動物よりも進化したのか。

ex.en: The male ape is intelligent by nature.
ex.ja: そのオスざるは生まれつき頭が良い。

note.ja: 古英語 apa（類人猿）から。「類人猿」→「まねる」。

en: One who audits bookkeeping accounts.
In many jurisdictions, an elected or appointed public official in charge of the public accounts; a comptroller.

auditor.ety: From Anglo-Norman auditour, from Latin audītor (“hearer, auditor”).

note.ja: ラテン語 auditor（聞く人）から。audire（聞く）。昔は帳簿を読み上げて聞いて確かめたことから「監査役」。audio と同じ。

en: A large mass or body of snow and ice sliding swiftly down a mountain side, or falling down a precipice.
A fall of earth, rocks, etc., similar to that of an avalanche of snow or ice.
To descend like an avalanche.
To come down upon; to overwhelm.

avalanche.ety: From French avalanche, from Franco-Provençal (Savoy) avalançhe, blend of aval (“downhill”) and standard lavençhe, from Vulgar Latin *labanka (compare Occitan lavanca, Italian valanga), of uncertain origin, perhaps an alteration of Late Latin lābīna (“landslide”) (compare Franco-Provençal (Dauphiné) lavino, Romansh lavina), from Latin lābēs, from lābor (“to slip, slide”).

ex.en: The road was blocked by an avalanche.
ex.ja: 雪崩で道路がふさがった。

ex.en: That's the fact that avalanches occur after mountain fires.
ex.ja: それは山火事の後に「土石流」が発生するということです。

ex.en: You have to watch out for avalanches at this time of the year.
ex.ja: 今頃の時期はなだれに注意しなければならない。

note.ja: スイスのフランス語 lavanche が avaler（下る）の影響で変化した語。「雪崩」→「殺到」。

en: Any member of species of the genera Meles, Arctonyx, Mellivora or Taxidea, of mammals.
A native or resident of the American state, Wisconsin.
To pester; to annoy persistently; to press.

badger.ety: From Middle English bageard (“marked by a badge”), from bage (“badge”), referring to the animal's badge-like white blaze, equivalent to badge + -ard. Displaced earlier brock, from Old English brocc.

ex.en: Even a rabbit, if badgered into a corner, will fight back.
ex.ja: ウサギでさえ、いじめられて片隅に追いつめられると、刃向かってくるだろう。

ex.en: Badgers dig deep holes.
ex.ja: アナグマは深い穴を掘る。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。badge（顔の白い印）と関係するとされる。犬にアナグマを追わせた遊びから「しつこくせがむ」。

en: Of or relating to ballistics.
Of or relating to projectiles moving under their own momentum, aerodynamic drag, gravity, and sometimes rocket power, without significant…

ballistic.ety:
Etymology tree

Ancient Greek βαλλίστρᾱ (ballístrā)bor.

English ballistic
Learned borrowing from New Latin ballisticus, from Classical Latin ballista (“ballista, a military siege engine for throwing stones”) + -icus (adjectival suffix). By surface analysis, ballista + -ic.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ballein（投げる）から。「投げる物の」→「弾道の」。problem、symbol と同じ ballein。

en: Sharp, good-humoured, playful, typically spontaneous conversation.
Good-humoured bits of monologue and/or conversational prompts used in any of a wide range of occupations that must frequently interact wi…
To engage in banter or playful conversation.
To play or do something amusing.

banter.ety: 1670s as verb, 1680s as noun. The origin is unknown, possibly from London street slang; ostensibly as *bant + -er (frequentative suffix). Possibly an Anglo-Gaelicism from the Irish bean (“woman”), so that "banter" means "talk of women."

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。17世紀のロンドンの俗語。「冗談のやりとり」。

en: Someone who bids (all senses), but most commonly, one offers to pay a specified price at an auction.
One who commands or orders.

bidder.ety: From Middle English bidder, biddere, equivalent to bid + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Bidder, German Bitter.

en: A high-explosive bomb used for the purposes of demolishing extensive areas, such as a city block.
Something, such as a film or book, that sustains exceptional and widespread popularity and achieves enormous sales, as opposed to a box o…

blockbuster.ety: From block + buster, referring originally to aerial bombs capable of destroying a whole block of buildings.

note.ja: block（街区）+ buster（壊すもの）。第二次大戦で街区ごと吹き飛ばす爆弾 →「大ヒット作」。

en: A type of paper-based reproduction process producing white-on-blue images by means of a photosensitive ferric compound, used primarily fo…
A print produced with this process.
To make a blueprint for.
To make a detailed operational plan for; to design or plan out.

blueprint.ety: From blue + print. Introduced by Sir John Herschel in 1842.

ex.en: The spokesman explained the blueprint of the scheme to the press.
ex.ja: 報道担当官がその計画の青写真を報道陣に説明した。

ex.en: These measurements conform to the blueprints.
ex.ja: これらの寸法は設計図に一致する。

note.ja: blue（青）+ print（印刷）。昔の設計図が青焼きだったことから「青写真・設計図」。

zh: 保齡球運動員 /保龄球运动员

en: One who engages in the sport of bowling.
The player currently bowling.

note.ja: bowl（ボールを投げる）+ -er。「投手・ボウリングをする人」。帽子の bowler は帽子屋の名から。

en: A piece of jewelry, etc., carved in relief.
A single very brief appearance, especially by a prominent celebrity in a movie or song.
To appear in a cameo role.

cameo.ety: Borrowed from Italian cammeo, from Medieval Latin camaeus, of unknown origin. The movie sense is short for “cameo role” referring to a famous person who was playing no character, but him or herself. Like a cameo brooch — a low-relief carving of a person’s head or bust — the actor or celebrity is instantly recognizable. More recently, it has come to refer to any short appearances, whether as a character or as oneself. Doublet of camaieu.

note.ja: イタリア語 cammeo から。語源ははっきりしない。小さく浮き彫りにした肖像 →「（有名人の）ちょい役」。

en: A smooth, chewy, sticky confection made by heating sugar and other ingredients until the sugars polymerize and become sticky.
A (sometimes hardened) piece of this confection.
Of a yellow-brown color.

caramel.ety: Borrowed from French caramel, from Spanish caramelo, from Portuguese caramelo, dissimilated from Late Latin calamellus, diminutive of calamus (“reed”) (and a doublet of chalumeau and shawm). Alternatively from Medieval Latin cannamellis, which is a compound of canna + mellis.

ex.en: Can I eat some caramel ice cream?
ex.ja: キャラメルアイスクリームを食べてもいい？

ex.en: Can I have some caramel ice cream?
ex.ja: キャラメルアイスクリームを食べてもいい？

ex.en: Can I eat caramel ice cream?
ex.ja: キャラメルアイス食べてもいい？

note.ja: スペイン語 caramelo から。ラテン語 calamellus（小さな葦）とされる。

en: Of, related to, or having charisma: having a form of compelling charm or personality which inspires devotion in others; charming, fascina…
Of, related to, or being a member of a form of Christianity that emphasizes the role of the Holy Spirit.
A member of the Charismatic Movement.

charismatic.ety: From Ancient Greek χάρισμα (khárisma, “grace, favour, gift”) + -ic.

ex.en: He's so cool that we all think he's charismatic.
ex.ja: 彼ってクールだから、私たちみんな彼にはカリスマ性があると思っている。

ex.en: Tom said he thought I was charismatic.
ex.ja: 僕はカリスマ的だと思ったとトムは言った。

ex.en: She has finally been regarded by the nation as the most charismatic actress.
ex.ja: 彼女はついに最もカリスマ性のある女優として国民から認められました。

en: A linear arrangement of condensed DNA and associated proteins (such as chaperone proteins) which contains the genetic material (genome) o…

chromosome.ety: 19th century: from German Chromosom, ultimately from Ancient Greek χρῶμα (khrôma, “colour”) + σῶμα (sôma, “body”) (because they are stained under the microscope). Equivalent to chromo- + -some.

ex.en: The chromosomes in our cells contain the whole of our genetic material.
ex.ja: 私たちの細胞の染色体は遺伝物質のすべてを含んでいる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 khrōma（色）+ sōma（体）。染料でよく染まる体 →「染色体」。chrome（クロム）と同じ。

en: The first existence of anything; act or fact of commencing; the beginning.
The day when degrees are conferred by colleges and universities upon students and others.

commencement.ety: From French commencement; analyzable as commence + -ment.

note.ja: commence（始まる）+ -ment。「開始」→ 社会人生活の始まり →（米）「卒業式」。

en: To use one's authority to lay claim to and separate a possession from its holder.

confiscate.ety: Borrowed from Latin cōnfiscātus, the perfect passive participle of Latin cōnfiscō (“to seize for the public treasury (fiscus)”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix) and -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

ex.en: My license was confiscated.
ex.ja: 私の免許は没収になった。

ex.en: If you leave your textbooks at school during the break, they'll get confiscated.
ex.ja: 休み中に置き勉してると没収されるんだよな。

note.ja: ラテン語 confiscare（国庫に入れる）から。con + fiscus（かご・国庫）。fiscal（財政の）と同じ。

en: That contradicts something, such as an argument.
That is itself a contradiction.
Either of a pair of propositions, that cannot both be true or both be false.

contradictory.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin contradictorius, from Latin contradico. Equivalent to contradict + -ory.

ex.en: His statement sounds correct at first, but upon thinking carefully, you realize it's contradictory.
ex.ja: 彼の発言一見正しいように聞こえるが、よく考えると矛盾していることに気づく。

en: A religious community whose members live under strict observation of religious rules and self-imposed vows.
The buildings and pertaining surroundings in which such a community lives.

convent.ety: From Middle English convent, variant of covent, from Old French covent, from Latin conventus, perfect participle of the verb convenio (whence ultimately convene), see con- + venio. Doublet of coven.

en: To talk; to engage in conversation.
To keep company; to hold intimate intercourse; to commune.
Free verbal interchange of thoughts or views; conversation; chat.
Opposite; reversed in order or relation; reciprocal.

converse.ety: From Old French converser, from Latin conversor (“live, have dealings with”).

ex.en: What made you start conversing in English?
ex.ja: 英会話を始めたきっかけは何ですか？

ex.en: He conversed with those exchange students.
ex.ja: 彼はその交換留学生たちと話した。

ex.en: I hold the converse opinion.
ex.ja: 私は逆の意見を持っている。

note.ja: con（共に）+ vers（向ける）+ e。互いに向き合う →「会話する」、向きが逆の →「逆（の）」。

en: The act of corroding or the condition so produced.
A substance (such as rust) so formed.

corrosion.ety: From Middle English corrosioun, from Old French corrosion, or its source, Late Latin corrōsiōnem, accusative singular of corrōsiō (“gnawing away, corroding”), from Latin corrōdō (“gnaw away, corrode”).

note.ja: corrode（腐食する）+ -sion。cor（完全に）+ rodere（かじる）。「かじり取ること」→「腐食」。erosion と同じ rod。

en: A baby’s bed with high, often slatted, often moveable sides, suitable for a child who has outgrown a cradle or bassinet.
A bed for a child older than a baby.
To place or confine in a crib.
To shut up or confine in a narrow habitation; to cage; to cramp.

crib.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *grebʰ-der.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Kräbbe, Krääb, Krääf (“crib”)

ex.en: The baby in the crib is very cute.
ex.ja: ベビーベッドの赤ちゃん、めっちゃ可愛い。

ex.en: The baby is sleeping in his crib.
ex.ja: 赤ちゃんはベビーベッドで寝てます。

ex.en: Writing crib sheets is very useful.
ex.ja: カンペを作っとくと、すごく便利だよ。

note.ja: 古英語 cribb（まぐさおけ）から。「まぐさおけ」→ 柵のある「ベビーベッド」。

en: A place where one road crosses another; an intersection of two or more roads.
A centrally located position.

ex.en: The crossroads where the accident happened is near here.
ex.ja: 事故が起きた交差点はこの近くです。

ex.en: He came to an important crossroads in his life.
ex.ja: 彼は人生のターニングポイントに立っていた。

ex.en: A crossroads is where two roads meet in an X.
ex.ja: 四つ角は二つの道が十字に交わった所である。

note.ja: cross（交わる）+ roads（道）。「交差点」→「岐路」。

en: In a dear or precious manner.
In a dear or expensive manner.

dearly.ety: From Middle English derely, deorliche, from Old English dēorlīċe (“worthily, richly”), equivalent to dear + -ly.

ex.en: Love your parents as dearly as your parents love you.
ex.ja: 親があなたを思うのと同じように親を思いなさい。

ex.en: She is dearly loved by everybody.
ex.ja: 彼女はみんなから深く愛されている。

ex.en: His success was purchased dearly.
ex.ja: 彼の成功は大きな犠牲をはらって勝ち得たものであった。

en: The feeling, or spirit of being defiant.
Open or bold resistance to or disregard for authority, opposition, or power; refusing to give up.

defiance.ety: From Middle English defiaunce, from Old French desfiance, from desfier. By surface analysis, defy + -ance.

ex.en: She got married in defiance of her father.
ex.ja: 彼女は父の意に逆らって結婚した。

ex.en: His brazen act of defiance almost cost him his life.
ex.ja: その恥知らずな抵抗活動のために、彼は危うく命を失いかけた。

ex.en: He hurled defiance at me.
ex.ja: あいつが俺に向かって啖呵を切った。

note.ja: defy（逆らう）+ -ance。de（離れて）+ fidare（信頼する）。「忠誠を捨てること」→「反抗」。confide と同じ fid。

en: To prevent something from happening.
To persuade someone not to do something; to discourage.

deter.ety: Borrowed from Latin dēterreō (“deter, discourage”), from de (“from”) + terreō (“to frighten”).

ex.en: His sudden illness deterred us from traveling.
ex.ja: 彼の急病で旅行は取りやめになった。

note.ja: de（離れて）+ terrere（怖がらせる）。「怖がらせて遠ざける」→「抑止する」。terror と同じ。

en: Someone who dines.
A car in a railroad train that serves meals.

ex.en: My favorite restaurant is Chuck's Diner.
ex.ja: 一番好きな飲食店はチャックス・ダイナーだよ。

ex.en: Chuck's Diner has closed.
ex.ja: チャックス・ダイナーは閉店しました。

ex.en: Tom usually eats lunch at Chuck's Diner.
ex.ja: トムはいつもはチャックス・ダイナーで昼食をとってるよ。

note.ja: dine（食事をする）+ -er。「食事客」→ 食堂車風の「簡易食堂」。

en: The arrangement or placement of certain things.
Control over something, especially with regard to disposing or dispensing with an action item (disposal of a concern, allocation of disbu…
To remove or place in a different position.

disposition.ety: From Middle English disposicioun, from Middle French disposition, from Latin dispositiōnem, accusative singular of dispositiō, from dispōnō. By surface analysis, dispose + -ition. Doublet of dispositio.

ex.en: He has a sociable disposition.
ex.ja: 彼は社交的な性格だ。

ex.en: She shows a shy disposition.
ex.ja: 彼女は内気な性格の持ち主です。

ex.en: He is obstinate in disposition.
ex.ja: 彼は性質が頑固だ。

note.ja: dis（あちこちに）+ pos（置く）+ ition。配置のしかた →「性質・気質・配置」。

en: Intense pleasure.
A state of emotion so intense that a person is carried beyond rational thought and self-control.
To experience intense pleasure.
To cause intense pleasure in.

ecstasy.ety: From Old French estaise (“ecstasy, rapture”), from Latin ecstasis, from Ancient Greek ἔκστασις (ékstasis), from ἐξίστημι (exístēmi, “to displace”), from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

ex.en: She went into ecstasies about the ring he had bought her.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼が買ってくれた指輪で有頂天になっていた。

ex.en: Ecstasy is a stimulant type of drug.
ex.ja: エクスタシーはアッパー系のドラッグだ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 ekstasis（自分の外に立つこと）＝ ek + histanai（立つ）。「我を忘れること」→「恍惚」。

en: The ordinal form of the number eighteen.
The person or thing in the eighteenth position.
One of eighteen equal parts of a whole.

eighteenth.ety: Inherited from Middle English eightetenthe, eightetethe, from Old English eahtatēoþa, from Proto-Germanic *ahtudô tehundô. Equivalent to eighteen + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: We're going to the party in eighteenth century costumes.
ex.ja: 私たちは１８世紀の衣装を着てそのパーティーに行きます。

ex.en: Fashion in the eighteenth century emphasized the bosom.
ex.ja: １８世紀の流行は胸の部分を強調していた。

note.ja: eighteen + -th。「18番目」。

ja: 11番目（の）（at the eleventh hour：土壇場で）

en: The ordinal form of the number eleven.
The person or thing in the eleventh position.
One of eleven equal parts of a whole.

eleventh.ety: From Middle English elleventhe, from elleven + -the, equivalent to eleven + -th. This re-formation replaced inherited forms such as ellefte, enlefte, from Old English endlefta, from Proto-Germanic *ainaliftô.

ex.en: November is the eleventh month of the year.
ex.ja: 「１１月」は１年の中で１１回目の月にあたります。

ex.en: We'd better finish up this project before the eleventh hour.
ex.ja: 土壇場になる前にこのプロジェクトを終わらせたほうがいい。

ex.en: I'm in the eleventh grade.
ex.ja: 私は高校2年生だ。

note.ja: eleven + -th。「11番目」。eleven は「（10を数えて）1つ残る」の意。

en: A diplomatic agent of the second rank, next in status after an ambassador.
A representative.

envoy.ety: From French envoyé (“envoy, messenger”), from envoyer (“send”).

note.ja: フランス語 envoyer（送る）から。ラテン語 inviare（道に送り出す）、via（道）。「使節」。

en: The act or process of breathing out, or forcing air from the lungs through the nose or mouth.
A single outward breath.

expiration.ety: From Middle English expiracioun, exspiracioun (“vapor, breath”), from Latin expīrātiōnem, exspīrātiōnem, accusative singular of expīrātiō, exspīrātiō. By surface analysis, expire + -ation.

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ (s)pir（息をする）+ ation。最後の息を吐き出すこと →「満了・期限切れ・呼気」。expire（期限が切れる）。

en: In an express or explicit manner; in a clear or specific manner.
Exclusively or specifically.

expressly.ety:
Etymology tree
English express
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English expressly
From express + -ly.

note.ja: express（はっきりした）+ -ly。ex（外へ）+ premere（押す）。「押し出して示す」→「はっきりと」。

en: The act of fabricating, framing, or constructing; construction; manufacture
That which is fabricated; a falsehood.

fabrication.ety: From Middle French fabrication, from Latin fabricatio. Equivalent to fabricate + -ion.

note.ja: fabricate（作る・でっち上げる）+ -ion。ラテン語 fabrica（作業場）。「製造・でっち上げ」。

en: The state or condition of being fascinated.
Something which fascinates.

fascination.ety: From Latin fascinare ("to bewitch"), possibly from Ancient Greek βασκαίνιεν (baskaínien, “to speak ill of; to curse”). Morphologically fascinate + -ion.

ex.en: I can't run away from the fascination of music.
ex.ja: 私は音楽の魅力から逃れることはできない。

ex.en: I have a fascination with the state-of-the-art A.I. research.
ex.ja: 人工知能の最先端の研究は私を蠱惑する。

note.ja: fascinate（魅了する）+ -ion。ラテン語 fascinare（魔法をかける）。「魅了」。

en: A conifer of the genus Abies.
Any pinaceous conifer of related genera, especially a Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga) or a Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris).

fir.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *perkʷ-der.
Proto-Germanic *furhō
Proto-West Germanic *furhu
Old English furh
Middle English firre
English fir
From Middle English firre, from Old English fyrh, furh, as in furhwudu (“pinewood”), from Proto-West Germanic *furhu, from Proto-Germanic *furhō, *furhijǭ, from Proto-Indo-European *pŕ̥kʷeh₂, from *pérkʷus (“oak”). Possibly conflated during Middle English with Old Norse fýri (as in fýriskógr (“pine-wood”).
Germanic cognates include Dutch vuren, Low German Fuhr, German Föhre (“pine”), Danish fyr). Outside of Germanic, compare Italian (Trentino) porca

ex.en: That's not a fir tree.
ex.ja: それって、もみの木とちゃうよ。

ex.en: The child climbed to the top of the fir tree.
ex.ja: その子はモミの木の上に登った。

note.ja: 古英語 fyrh から。「モミ」。

en: The act, process, or result of formulating or reducing to a formula.
A particular linguistic construction; a turn of phrase.

note.ja: formulate（定式化する）+ -ion。ラテン語 formula（小さな型）、forma。「策定・配合」。

en: Any of several units of currency.

franc.ety: Borrowed from French franc. Doublet of Frank, frank, and farang.

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 Francorum rex（フランク人の王）と刻まれた硬貨から。「フラン」。France、frank と同じ。

en: Of, relating to, directed toward, or situated at the front.
Directed against the front or at the main point or issue.
A decorative drapery covering the front of an altar.
The façade of a building.

frontal.ety: Borrowed from New Latin frontālis, from frons (“the forehead, brow, front”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix), equivalent to front + -al; cognate of French frontal. Doublet of frontalis.

en: A goalkeeper or goaltender.
To act as a goalie, to tend the goals, to mind the net.
A slope or incline.
A rate of inclination or declination of a slope.
Moving by steps; walking.
Rising or descending by regular degrees of inclination.

gradient.ety: From Latin gradiēns, present participle of gradior (“to step, to walk”).

ex.en: The gradient of this hill is steep.
ex.ja: この坂の勾配が大きい。

note.ja: ラテン語 gradi（歩む）の現在分詞。「段階的に変わるもの」→「勾配・グラデーション」。grade、graduate と同じ grad。

en: A dark savoury sauce prepared from stock and usually meat juices; brown gravy.
A pale sauce prepared from a roux with meat fat; a type of béchamel sauce.
To make gravy.

gravy.ety:
From Middle English gravey, greavie, gravy; probably from greaves, graves (“the sediment of melted tallow”), or from Old French grave, a claimed misspelling of grané (“stew, spice”), from grain (“spice”).
Sense of "pasta sauce" apparently seems to be from Italian dialect, especially Calabrian, differentiating tomato puree (salsa (“sauce”)) from cooked tomato sauce (sugo).

ex.en: Would you like some more gravy?
ex.ja: グレイビーをもう少しいかがですか。

ex.en: Is there enough gravy?
ex.ja: ソースは足りてますか？

note.ja: 古フランス語 grané（穀粒で味つけしたソース）の写し間違いとされる。「肉汁ソース」。

ja: ニシン（red herring：人の気をそらすもの）

en: A type of small, oily fish of the genus Clupea, often used as food.
Fish in the family Clupeidae.

herring.ety: From Middle English hering, from Old English hǣring, from Proto-West Germanic *hāring (“herring”), further etymology unknown. Possibly derived from Proto-Germanic *hērą (“hair”) + -ing, due to the similarity of their fine bones to hair. Cognate with Scots hering, haring (“herring”), Saterland Frisian Hiering, Häiring (“herring”), West Frisian hjerring (“herring”), Dutch haring (“herring”), German Low German Hereng, Hering (“herring”), German Hering (“herring”), Bavarian Haring (“herring”). Late Latin haringus (whence French hareng, etc.) is borrowed from Germanic.

ex.en: What she liked best was herring roe.
ex.ja: 彼女が最も気に入ったのは数の子でした。

ex.en: The police followed a red herring while they let the true criminal escape.
ex.ja: 警察が追っていたのは替え玉で、その間に真犯人を逃してしまった。

note.ja: 古英語 hǣring から。「ニシン」。red herring（燻製ニシン）は猟犬の訓練でにおいをそらすのに使ったことから「人の気をそらすもの」。

en: Of, or arising from hysteria.
Having, or prone to having hysterics.

hysterical.ety: From hysteric + -al, from Latin hystericus, from Ancient Greek ὑστερικός (husterikós, “suffering in the womb, hysterical”), from ῠ̔στέρᾱ (hŭstérā, “womb”).

ex.en: I get hysterical easily.
ex.ja: すぐにヒステリーになります。

en: Of two or more things: that cannot coexist; not congruous because of differences; unable to function together due to dissimilarities.
Incapable of being together without mutual reaction or decomposition, as certain medicines.
An incompatible substance; one of a group of things that cannot be placed or used together because of a change of chemical composition or…
A consequent of a contrary.

ex.en: Our managing director is incompatible with the president.
ex.ja: 専務は社長とうまくいっていない。

ex.en: His desires are incompatible with his income.
ex.ja: 彼の欲望は収入とつりあわない。

note.ja: in（否定）+ compatible（両立できる）。com + pati（耐える・感じる）。「共に耐えられない」→「両立しない」。patient と同じ。

en: The act of enjoining; the act of directing, commanding, or prohibiting.
That which is enjoined; such as an order, mandate, decree, command, precept.

injunction.ety: From Middle English iniunccyon, iniunccion, from Old French injonctïon, from Latin iniūnctiō (“command, injunction”).

en: Inborn; existing or having existed since birth.
Originating in, or derived from, the constitution of the intellect, as opposed to acquired from experience.

innate.ety: The adjective is first attested in the 1420s, the verb in 1602; from Middle English innat(e) (“innate, inborn”), borrowed from Latin innātus (“inborn, innate”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix)), perfect active participle of innāscor (“to be born in, grow up in”), from in- (“in, at on”) + nāscor (“to be born”); see natal, native. The verb is derived from the adjective, see -ate (verb-forming suffix).

ex.en: She has an innate love of adventure.
ex.ja: 彼女は根っからの冒険家だ。

ex.en: He has an innate love of adventure.
ex.ja: 彼は生まれつき冒険家だ。

ex.en: Tom has an innate talent.
ex.ja: トムには持って生まれた才能がある。

note.ja: in（中に）+ nat（生まれる）+ e。生まれつき中にある →「生まれつきの・先天的な」。

en: A speech that sets the main theme of a conference or other gathering; a keynote speech or keynote address.
The main theme of a speech, a written work, or a conference.
To deliver a speech that sets the main theme of a conference or other gathering.

note.ja: key（鍵・音の調）+ note（音）。「（曲の）主音」→「基調・主眼」。

en: To seize or detain (a person) unlawfully and transport or conceal them, sometimes for ransom.
The crime, or an instance, of kidnapping.

kidnap.ety: From kid + nap (“to nab; to grab”). Originally Thieves' cant, referring to the practice of stealing children and shipping them to colonies or plantations as laborers. First attested c. 1680.

ex.en: That child may have been kidnapped on his way home.
ex.ja: その子は帰宅の途中で誘拐されたのかもしれない。

ex.en: The girl has been kidnapped.
ex.ja: その女の子、誘拐されちゃったんだ。

ex.en: The girl was kidnapped.
ex.ja: その女の子、誘拐されちゃったんだ。

note.ja: kid（子ども）+ nap（さらう）。「誘拐する」。kidnapping と同じ。

en: A master of Tibetan Buddhism.

lama.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Sino-Tibetan
Tibetan བླ (bla)
Tibetan མ (ma)
Tibetan བླ་མ (bla ma)bor.
English lama
Borrowed from Tibetan བླ་མ (bla ma).

note.ja: チベット語 bla-ma（上に立つ者）から。「ラマ僧」。動物のラマ（llama）は別語。

learner.ety:

ex.en: Never forget that you too were once a learner.
ex.ja: 初心、忘るべからず。

ex.en: This sentence isn't useful for language learners.
ex.ja: この文は、語学学習者には役に立たないよ。

ex.en: He cannot be a slow learner.
ex.ja: 彼は覚えが遅いはずがない。

note.ja: learn（学ぶ）+ -er。「学習者」。

en: Tending or intended to motivate.

motivational.ety:
Etymology tree
Anglo-Norman motifder.
Middle French motifder.

English motivation

Proto-Indo-Eu

note.ja: motivation（動機づけ）+ -al。ラテン語 movere（動かす）。「やる気を起こさせる」。motive、motion と同じ mov。

en: Happening or appearing in the night; night-time; nocturnal.
Performing, occurring, or taking place every night.
Every night.
A build of a software program with the latest changes, released every night.

nightly.ety: From Middle English nyȝtly, nihtlich, nihtlic, from Old English nihtlīċ, nihtelīċ (“nocturnal, nightly, of the night, at night”), equivalent to night + -ly. Cognate with Scots nichtlie (“nightly”), West Frisian nachtlik (“nightly, nocturnal”), Dutch nachtelijk (“nightly, nocturnal”), German nächtlich (“nocturnal, nightly”), Danish natlig (“nightly”), Swedish nattlig (“nightly, nocturnal”).

ex.en: The policeman was on his usual nightly round.
ex.ja: 巡査はいつものように夜間の巡回中だった。

en: Nevertheless, all the same.
Although; despite the fact that; even though.
In spite of, despite.

notwithstanding.ety: From Middle English notwithstandinge, notwithstondyng, natwithstandyng, equivalent to not + withstanding. Compare Middle English notgainstonding, not aȝenstondynge, of similar meaning and formation.

ex.en: She accepted our offer notwithstanding.
ex.ja: それにもかかわらず彼女は私たちの言い値を受け入れた。

ex.en: He failed notwithstanding my advice.
ex.ja: 私の忠告にも関わらず彼は失敗した。

ex.en: Notwithstanding their own repeated scandals, the police continue to nonchalantly issue infringement tickets.
ex.ja: 相次ぐ不祥事にも関わらず、警察はオメオメ違反切符を切っている。

en: Established by authority.
Admitted to the ministry of the church.

ex.en: God has ordained that all men shall die.
ex.ja: 神は人間はみな死ぬものと定めた。

en: The complete loss of voluntary control of part of a living body, such as one or more limbs.
A state of being unable to act.

paralysis.ety: Borrowed from Latin paralysis, from Ancient Greek παράλυσις (parálusis, “palsy”), from παραλύω (paralúō, “to disable on one side”). By surface analysis, para- + -lysis. Doublet of palsy.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paralysis（体の片側の弛緩）から。para（そばに）+ lyein（ほどく）。「麻痺」。analysis と同じ lyein。

en: In a patient manner.

patiently.ety:
Etymology tree
English patient
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English patiently
From patient + -ly.

ex.en: I listen patiently, but without interest.
ex.ja: 根気強く聞いてはいるけど、興味はない。

ex.en: He was angry, but he listened to me patiently.
ex.ja: 彼は怒っていたが、私のいうことをがまんして聞いた。

ex.en: He was patiently digging for facts.
ex.ja: 彼はこつこつ事実を調べていた。

en: The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
Of an animal, to dig through (something, such as a garbage can) with paws.
Of an animal, to draw the forefoot along the ground; to beat or scrape with the forefoot.

paw.ety:
From Middle English pawe, from Old French poue, poe, from Vulgar Latin *pauta. Further origin unknown, perhaps from Frankish *pōta, from Frankish *pōtōn (“to put, stick, plant”), from Proto-Germanic *putōną, whence also Old English potian (“to push”), pȳtan (“to put out, poke out”). See more at put. Doublet of pote, put, and putt.
Cognate with Dutch poot, poten (“to plant”), Low German Pote, German Pfote, Icelandic pota (“to stick”).

ex.en: Get your dirty paws off me.
ex.ja: 私に触らないで。

ex.en: The cat likes fish, but doesn't like getting its paws wet.
ex.ja: その猫は魚が好きなんだけど、足が濡れるのが嫌なのよ。

ex.en: I saw a dog with one paw bandaged.
ex.ja: 私は片足に包帯を巻いた犬を見た。

note.ja: 古フランス語 poue（足）から。「（動物の）足」。

en: A person who plays the piano, particularly with skill or as part of an orchestra.
A spy using radio or wireless telegraphy to keep in touch with headquarters during the Second World War.

pianist.ety: From French pianiste, from Italian pianista. Analyzable as piano + -ist.

ex.en: She has a daughter who is a pianist.
ex.ja: 彼女にはピアニストをしている娘がいる。

ex.en: The pianist played a trick on the audience.
ex.ja: ピアニストは聴衆をだました。

ex.en: As a pianist, he is far above me.
ex.ja: ピアニストとしては彼は私よりはるかに優れている。

note.ja: piano + -ist。piano は pianoforte（弱く強く弾ける楽器）の短縮。

en: Any traveler.
An early American settler.
To make a pilgrimage

pilgrim.ety:
Inherited from Middle English pilegrim, from Old English pilegrī̆m, from Old French pelegrin, from Latin peregrīnus (“foreigner”). Doublet of peregrine.
The change of /r…r/ to /l…r/ is an effect of dissimilation in early Romance; compare Italian pellegrino.

ex.en: I decided to go away with the pilgrims.
ex.ja: 遍路さんたちと一緒に去る事に決めた。

ex.en: The party of pilgrims started for Shikoku.
ex.ja: お遍路さんの一行は四国に向かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 peregrinus（よそ者）から。per + ager（土地）。「土地を越えて旅する人」→「巡礼者」。

en: A dummy medicine containing no active ingredients; an inert treatment.
The vespers sung in the office for the dead.

placebo.ety: Inherited from Middle English placebo, borrowed from Latin placēbō (“I will please”), the first-person singular future active indicative of placeō (“to please”).

note.ja: ラテン語で「私は喜ばせよう」。placere（喜ばせる）。患者を安心させるための薬 →「偽薬」。please と同じ。

en: To delay or put off an event, appointment, etc.

postpone.ety: From Latin postpōnō (“to put after; to postpone”) from post (“after”) + pōnō (“to put; to place”), compare forestall.

ex.en: I've decided to postpone my trip to Australia.
ex.ja: オーストラリア旅行は延期することにしたよ。

ex.en: I've decided to postpone my trip to Boston.
ex.ja: ボストンへの旅行は延期することにしたよ。

ex.en: Why don't we postpone this until next week?
ex.ja: これ、来週に延期しない？

note.ja: post（後に）+ pon（置く）+ e。後ろに置く →「延期する」。

en: In a progressive manner.
As part of a progression.

progressively.ety:
Etymology tree
English progressive
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English progressively
From progressive + -ly.

ex.en: The situation is growing progressively worse.
ex.ja: 状況はどんどん悪化してます。

en: To provide an impetus for motion or physical action; to cause to move in a certain direction; to drive or push forward.
To provide an impetus for nonphysical change; to cause to arrive to a certain situation or result.

propel.ety: From Middle English propellen (“drive out, expel”), from Latin propellō, from pro- (“forward”) and pellō (“to push, to move”).

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ pellere（押す）。「前へ押す」→「推進する」。propeller、compel と同じ pel。

en: A narrow shallow boat, square at both ends, traditionally propelled by a pole.
To propel a punt or similar craft by means of a pole.
Of a fish, to walk along the seafloor using its fins as limbs.

punt.ety: From Old English punt, from Latin pontō (“Gaulish flat-bottomed boat, pontoon”), from pons (“bridge”); readopted from Middle Low German punte (“ferry boat”) or Middle Dutch ponte (“ferry boat”) of the same origin.

en: The act, process, or state of reinforcing or being reinforced.
A thing that reinforces.

reinforcement.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English inforce
English reinforce
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥tom
Proto-Italic *-mentom
Latin -mentum
Old French -mentbor.
Middle English -ment
English -ment
English reinforcement
From reinforce + -ment.

note.ja: reinforce（強化する）+ -ment。「強化・増援」。

en: The act or an instance of repeating or being repeated.
The act of performing a single, controlled exercise motion. A group of repetitions is a set.
To petition again.

repetition.ety: Borrowed from Latin repetitionem (accusative singular of repetitio; cf. French répétition). Doublet of repetitio. By surface analysis, repeat + -ition.

ex.en: Repetition plays an important role in language study.
ex.ja: 言葉の学習には繰り返しが必要です。

ex.en: Repetition helps you remember something.
ex.ja: 繰り返すことが物事を覚えるのに役に立つ。

ex.en: Every successful repetition spoke favorably for the quality of the first test.
ex.ja: うまく行われれば何回実験を繰り返しても、最初の実験の質が十分保証されるのだった。

note.ja: re（再び）+ pet（求める）+ ition。何度も求めること →「繰り返し・反復」。repeat（繰り返す）。

ja: 抑制する（restraining order：接近禁止命令）

en: The act by which someone or something is restrained.

ex.en: She is restraining the boy.
ex.ja: 彼女は男の子を引き止める。

en: Of, relating to, or contemplating the past.
Looking backwards.
An exhibition of works from an extended period of an artist's activity.

retrospective.ety: From retrospect + -ive. From Latin retrōspectus, perfect passive participle of retrōspiciō (“to look back at”).

note.ja: retro（後ろへ）+ spectare（見る）+ -ive。「振り返って見る」→「回顧的な・回顧展」。spectator と同じ spec。

en: The quality or state of being righteous.
Holiness; conformity of life to the divine law.

righteousness.ety: Corruption of earlier rightwiseness, from Middle English rightwisnes, from Old English rihtwīsnes (“justice”). By surface analysis, righteous + -ness.

ex.en: Education is the path to happiness, peace, righteousness, and success.
ex.ja: 教育は幸福と平和と正義と、そして勝利の道なのであります。

note.ja: righteous（正しい）+ -ness。「正義」。

en: To wash (something) quickly using water and no soap.
To remove soap from (something) using water.
The action of rinsing.
A liquid used to rinse, now particularly a hair dye.

rinse.ety:
From Middle English rinsen, rincen, rencen (“to rinse”), from Old French rincier, reinser, Old Northern French raïncer (“to rinse, cleanse”). Of contested origin. Possibly from Old Norse hreinsa, from Proto-Germanic *hrainisōną (“to clean, purify”), from Proto-Indo-European *krey- (“to separate, divide”). Alternatively from a dissimilation of Old French recincier, from Latin recentare (“to make fresh”).
Cognate with French rincer. From the Germanic verb are Danish rense, Norwegian rense, Swedish rensa (all “to clean”), Old High German reinisōn (“to clean, purify, atone”). It is related to Germ

ex.en: I have to rinse out my mouth.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

ex.en: I have to rinse my mouth out.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

ex.en: I have to rinse my mouth.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rincer（すすぐ）から。「すすぐ」。

en: The part of the head where the hair grows from, or used to grow from.
A part of the skin of the head, with the hair attached, formerly cut or torn off from an enemy by warriors in some cultures as a token of…
To remove the scalp (part of the head from where the hair grows), by brutal act or accident.
To bet on opposing competitors so as to make a profit from the bookmaker.

scalp.ety: From Middle English scalp, skalp, scalpe (“crown of the head; skull”). Originally a northern word, and therefore probably from a North Germanic source, although the sense-development is unclear; compare Sylt North Frisian Skolp (“dandruff”), Old Norse skálpr (“sheath”), Old Swedish skalp, Dutch schelp (“shell”).

ex.en: My scalp is very itchy.
ex.ja: 頭皮がかゆいのです。

note.ja: 北欧語 skalpr（さや）から。「頭皮」。

en: One who shuts or closes something.
Each of a series of protective panels, usually wooden, placed over windows to block out the light.
To close shutters covering.
To close up (a building) for a prolonged period of inoccupancy.

ex.en: It's about time to replace these shutters.
ex.ja: この雨戸もそろそろ取り替え時ね。

ex.en: I forgot to open the shutter.
ex.ja: シャッター開けるの忘れてた。

ex.en: I forgot to open the shutters.
ex.ja: シャッター開けるの忘れてた。

note.ja: shut（閉める）+ -er。「閉めるもの」→「よろい戸・シャッター」。

en: The full width of an open hand from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger used as an informal unit of length.
Any of various traditional units of length approximating this distance, especially the English handspan of 9 inches forming ⅛ fathom and …
To extend across (a gap or space between two sides).
To cover or extend over (an area or distance).

span.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend-der.
Proto-Germanic *spannō
Old English spann
Middle English spanne
English span
From Middle English spanne, from Old English spann, from Proto-Germanic *spannō (“span, handbreadth”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend- (“to stretch”).
Cognate with Dutch span, spanne, German Spanne. The sense “pair of horses” is probably from Old English ġespan, ġespann (“a joining; a fastening together; clasp; yoke”), from Proto-West Germanic [Term?]. Cognate with Dutch gespan, German Gespann.

ex.en: What is the average life span in Japan?
ex.ja: 日本での平均寿命はどれだけですか。

ex.en: The average life span of a dog is 10 years.
ex.ja: 犬の平均寿命は10年です。

ex.en: Young children have short attention spans.
ex.ja: 幼い子供は、注意力が続かないのです。

note.ja: 古英語 spann（手を広げた長さ）から。「範囲・期間」→「またがる」。

en: The house sparrow, Passer domesticus; a small bird with a short bill, and brown, white and gray feathers.
A member of the family Passeridae, comprising small Old World songbirds.

sparrow.ety:
From Middle English sparewe, sparowe, sparu, sparwe, spearewe, sperrewe, from Old English spearwa, from Proto-West Germanic *sparwō, from Proto-Germanic *sparwô, from Proto-Indo-European *spḗr (“sparrow”).
Cognates
Cognate with Yola sparrowe (“sparrow”), North Frisian sparag, spåri (“sparrow”), Saterland Frisian Spräie (“sparrow”), Alemannic German and Luxembourgish Spatz (“sparrow”), Dutch spreeuw (“starling”), German Spatz, Sperling (“sparrow”), Vilamovian śpielik, śpjelik, śpjeliḱ (“sparrow”), Yiddish שפּערל (shperl, “sparrow”), Danish and Norwegian Bokmål spurv (“sparrow”), Faroese spurvur

ex.en: Not a single sparrow was to be heard.
ex.ja: スズメの鳴き声一つしなかった。

ex.en: That bird is probably a sparrow.
ex.ja: あの鳥は、多分スズメだよ。

ex.en: A sparrow is very alert in its movements.
ex.ja: 雀は動作が非常にすばしこい。

note.ja: 古英語 spearwa から。「スズメ」。

en: To make an inference based on inconclusive evidence; to surmise or conjecture.
To make a risky trade in the hope of making a profit; to venture or gamble.

speculate.ety: Borrowed from Latin speculātus, perfect active participle of speculor (“to watch, observe, examine, spy”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from specula (“a watchtower”), ultimately from speciō (“to look at”).

ex.en: I am speculating that he may win the game.
ex.ja: 僕は彼が試合に勝つのではないかと推測している。

ex.en: He has been speculating on his future.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の将来について思い巡らせていた。

en: Any member of species Spinacia oleracea of edible plants, or its leaves.
Any of numerous plants, or their leaves, which are used for greens in the same way Spinacia oleracea is or resemble it in some way.

spinach.ety: From Middle English spinach, from Anglo-Norman spinache, from Old French espinoche, from Old Occitan espinarc, from Arabic إِسْفَانَاخ (ʔisfānāḵ), from Classical Persian اسپناخ (ispanāx, ispināx).

ex.en: There are people who don't like spinach.
ex.ja: ほうれん草が嫌いな人もいる。

ex.en: It seems like you really hate spinach.
ex.ja: 本当にほうれん草が嫌いみたいね。

ex.en: Tom knows that I hate spinach.
ex.ja: トムはね、私がほうれん草大嫌いなこと知ってるよ。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 aspanākh から、アラビア語・ラテン語を経た語。「ホウレンソウ」。

en: Relatively short or low, and thick or broad.
Sitting on one's heels; sitting close to the ground; cowering or crouching.
A position assumed by bending deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet.
Any of various modes of callisthenic exercises performed by moving the body and bending at least one knee.
To bend deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet.
To exercise by bending deeply at the knees and then rising, while bearing weight across the shoulders or upper back.

ex.en: Tom doesn't know squat about Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーについて何も知らない。

ex.en: 300 squats a day? That's completely impossible!
ex.ja: 1日300回のスクワット？そんなの絶対無理！

ex.en: Seen at a distance, the rock looks like a squatting human figure.
ex.ja: 少し離れて見ると、その岩は人がしゃがんだ姿に見える。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esquatir（押しつぶす）から。「しゃがむ」→ 空き家に居座る →「不法占拠する」。

en: A heated bath-room or steam-room; also, a hot bath.
A dish cooked by stewing.
To cook (food) by slowly boiling or simmering.
To brew (tea) for too long, so that the flavour becomes too strong.

stew.ety: From Middle English stewe, stue, from Anglo-Norman estouve, Old French estuve (“bath, bathhouse”) (modern French étuve), from Medieval Latin stupha, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Vulgar Latin *extufāre, from ex- + Ancient Greek τῦφος (tûphos, “smoke, steam”), from τύφω (túphō, “to smoke”). See also Italian stufare, Portuguese estufar. Compare also Old English stuf-bæþ (“a hot-air bath, vapour bath”); see stove.

ex.en: Could you give me a hand with this stew?
ex.ja: このシチューを作るの手伝ってくれないかしら。

ex.en: The stew was not half bad.
ex.ja: シチューは決して悪い味ではなかった。

ex.en: Sometimes I want to eat stew.
ex.ja: たまにシチューを食べたくなる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 estuver（湯気で温める）から。「とろとろ煮る」。stove と同系。

en: To heat (a substance) in a container so as to convert it into a gas which then condenses in solid form on cooler parts of the container; …
To raise (someone or an intangible thing) to a state of (especially moral or spiritual) excellence; to exalt.
Of an aspect of art or nature: causing awe or deep respect due to its beauty or magnificence; awe-inspiring, impressive.
Of flight: ascending, soaring.
An aspect of art or nature which causes awe or deep respect due to its beauty or magnificence; hence, the great beauty or magnificence of…
A style of language or writing which expresses opinions in a grand way.

sublime.ety:
PIE word
 *upó
Partly from the following:
* From Middle English sublimen, sublime, sublyme (“to exalt, extol, glorify, honour; (alchemy) to refine (a substance) by vaporizing in a closed container; to obtain (a substance) by cooling vapour obtained through sublimation; to extract (a pure substance) from a mixture by sublimation; to sublimate (a substance)”), from Middle French sublimer, Old French sublimer (“to exalt, glorify, honour; to refine (a substance) by vaporizing in a closed container; of a substance: to undergo sublimation”) (modern French sublimer), and from its etymon Latin sublīmā

ex.en: His death was a sublime self-sacrifice.
ex.ja: 彼の死は崇高な自己犠牲だった。

ex.en: It was sublime scenery.
ex.ja: それは崇高な光景であった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sublimis（高く掲げられた）から。sub（下から）+ limen（敷居・まぐさ）とされる。「崇高な」。

Textual versions of the dialogue in films (and similar media such as television or video games), usually displayed at the bottom of the s…
To create subtitles for the dialogue in a film.

ex.ja: トムは、フランス語の字幕付きで日本映画を見ました。

en: Belonging or relating to the branch of Islam based on the Qur'an, the Kutub al-Sittah (the hadiths which record the Sunnah) and that plac…
A follower of Sunni Islam.

Sunni.ety: From Arabic سُنِّيّ (sunniyy), from سُنَّة (sunna, “Sunna”) + ـِيّ (-iyy). By surface analysis, Sunna + -i.

note.ja: アラビア語 sunna（慣行・規範）から。「スンニ派」。

en: The condition of tasting sugary or tasting as if sugary, from either sugar or another sweet-tasting substance.
A pleasant disposition; kindness.

sweetness.ety: From Middle English swetnes, swetnesse, from Old English swētnes (“sweetness”), from Proto-West Germanic *swōtinassī (“sweetness”), equivalent to sweet + -ness. Cognate with West Frisian swietens (“sweetness”), obsolete Dutch zoetenis (“sweetness”), Old High German swuoznessi, suoznessi (“sweetness”).

note.ja: sweet（甘い）+ -ness。「甘さ・優しさ」。

en: The cooperative effort of a team of people to achieve a common goal.

teamwork.ety: From team + work. Compare West Frisian teamwurk (“teamwork”).

ex.en: The most wonderful thing about baseball is teamwork.
ex.ja: 野球の最もすばらしいところはチームワークだ。

ex.en: Each muscle shows perfect teamwork.
ex.ja: それぞれの筋肉が完璧なチームワークを示す。

ex.en: Teamwork is important in soccer.
ex.ja: サッカーは連携が大切だ。

note.ja: team（チーム）+ work（仕事）。「チームワーク」。

en: An alcoholic liquor distilled from the fermented juice of the Central American century plant Agave tequilana.

tequila.ety: Borrowed from Mexican Spanish tequila, from Tequila, a town in Jalisco.

ex.en: Tequila mixed with hot water also has a beautiful taste, it seems.
ex.ja: テキーラのお湯割りも美味しいらしい。

ex.en: I can't drink tequila.
ex.ja: テキーラは飲めないんだ。

ex.en: Tom is drinking tequila.
ex.ja: トムはテキーラを飲んでいる。

note.ja: メキシコの町テキーラ（Tequila）から。そこで作られた蒸留酒。

en: A ground-dwelling plant.
Of or relating to the Earth or its (native) inhabitants.
Of, relating to, or composed of land or earth, as contrasted with bodies of water, with wetlands viewed as semiaquatic environs, or with …

terrestrial.ety: From Middle English terrestrialle, from terrestre or Latin terrestris, from terra (“land, earth, ground”), with the suffix -al.

note.ja: terr（大地）+ estr + ial。大地の →「地球の・陸上の」。extraterrestrial（地球外の→宇宙人）。

en: One who spends time thinking, contemplating or meditating.
An intellectual, such as a philosopher or theologian.

thinker.ety: From Middle English thinkere, equivalent to think + -er. Compare West Frisian tinker (“thinker”), Dutch denker (“thinker”), German Denker (“thinker”), Danish tænker (“thinker”), Swedish tänkare (“thinker”).

ex.en: He is as great a thinker as ever lived.
ex.ja: 彼はまたとない優れた思想家である。

ex.en: Between you and me, he's a shallow thinker.
ex.ja: ここだけの話だが彼の考え方は深みに欠ける。

ex.en: Many great thinkers who were unknown while alive became famous after death.
ex.ja: 生前に無名であった多くの偉大な思想家は、死後に名声を得た。

note.ja: think（考える）+ -er。「思想家」。

ja: とげ（a thorn in one's side：悩みの種）

en: A modified branch that is hard and sharp like a spike.
Any thorn-like structure on plants, such as the spine and the prickle.
To pierce with, or as if with, a thorn (sharp pointed object).

thorn.ety:
From Middle English thorn, þorn, from Old English þorn, from Proto-West Germanic *þorn, from Proto-Germanic *þurnaz, from Proto-Indo-European *tr̥nós, from *(s)ter- (“stiff”).
Cognates
Near cognates include West Frisian toarn, Low German Doorn, Dutch doorn, German Dorn, Danish and Norwegian torn, Swedish torn, törne, Gothic 𐌸𐌰𐌿𐍂𐌽𐌿𐍃 (þaurnus). Further cognates include Old Church Slavonic трънъ (trŭnŭ, “thorn”), Russian тёрн (tjorn), Polish cierń, Kamkata-viri taňi, tai (“thorn”), Sanskrit तृण (tṛ́ṇa, “grass”).

ex.en: There is no rose without thorns.
ex.ja: 河豚は食いたし命は惜しし。

ex.en: Every rose has its thorn.
ex.ja: 河豚は食いたし命は惜しし。

ex.en: Just as a thorn stuck in one's throat.
ex.ja: 喉に刺さった棘の如く。

note.ja: 古英語 þorn（とげ）から。「とげ」→ a thorn in one's side（悩みの種）。

en: To remove a cover from.
To reveal the identity of.

uncover.ety: From Middle English uncoveren, equivalent to un- + cover.

en: Not natural.
Not occurring in nature, the environment or atmosphere

unnatural.ety: From Middle English unnatural, unnaturel, equivalent to un- + natural.

ex.en: She had an unnatural desire for money.
ex.ja: 彼女は金に対して異常なほど欲望を持っていた。

ex.en: This sentence sounds unnatural to me as an American.
ex.ja: この文章はアメリカ人の私には不自然に感じます。

ex.en: As an American, this sentence sounds unnatural to me.
ex.ja: この文章はアメリカ人の私には不自然に感じます。

note.ja: un（否定）+ natural（自然な）。「不自然な」。

ex.ja: 君の彼女への止められない気持ちは、愛でなくて何だろう。

en: Honest, frank and straightforward.
Open, admitted, out.
Beforehand.
As an attacker.
A meeting of network executives with the press and major advertisers, signaling the start of advertising sales for a new season.
To bring to the fore; to place up front for consideration.

note.ja: up（前に）+ front（前面）。「前もって・率直な」。

en: With great haste, with a sense of urgency, because it is very important.
Continuously. With insistence.

From urgent + -ly.

ex.ja: 見知らぬ人が玄関のドアをしきりにたたいた。

ex.en: Your prompt reply is urgently required.
ex.ja: あなたの迅速な返事が是非とも必要です。

note.ja: urgent（緊急の）+ -ly。ラテン語 urgere（迫る）。「緊急に」。

en: The state or characteristic of being a virgin.

virginity.ety: From Middle English virginite, from Old French virginite, from Latin virginitas. Equivalent to virgin + -ity. Displaced native Old English mæġeþhād (compare modern English maidhood), originally meaning “girlhood.”

ex.en: So? Feeling refreshed, the morning after graduating from virginity?
ex.ja: どーお？童貞卒業した翌朝は気分爽快？

note.ja: virgin（処女）+ -ity。ラテン語 virgo（乙女）。Virgo（おとめ座）と同じ。

en: A piece of paper or other token that entitles the holder to a discount, or that can be exchanged for goods and services.
A receipt.
To establish the authenticity of; to vouch for.
To provide a vouch for (an expenditure).

voucher.ety: From vouch + -er. The verb is from the noun.

note.ja: vouch（保証する）+ -er。ラテン語 vocare（呼ぶ）。「保証するもの」→「引換券」。voice と同じ voc。
